71939-gratitude.creator: Unknown
71939-gratitude.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. No one quite remembers when he arrived in Marook, or, at least, none ever mentioned it. Probably he came with that inrush in the late fall of ’97, when the newly discovered Klondike sent its refugees hurrying down the river to camps where they might be sure of supplies through the long winter season, and he laughed his way into a job as bartender, for want of something else to do, and then, in time, graduated to the post of running the roulette wheel

arxiv-1801-03176.title: The Fourier Restriction and Kakeya Problems over Rings of Integers Modulo N N
arxiv-1801-03176.creator: James Wright
arxiv-1801-03176.description: Abstract The Fourier restriction phenomenon and the size of Kakeya sets are explored in the setting of the ring of integers modulo N N for general N N and a striking similarity with the corresponding euclidean problems is observed. One should contrast this with known results in the finite field setting.

arxiv-1910-05568.title: Model-based process design of a ternary protein separation using multi-step gradient ion-exchange SMB chromatography
arxiv-1910-05568.creator: Qiao-Le He, Eric von Lieres, Zhaoxi Sun, Liming Zhao
arxiv-1910-05568.description: Abstract Model-based process design of ion-exchange simulated moving bed ( iex-smb ) chromatography for center-cut separation of proteins is studied. Use of nonlinear binding models that describe more accurate adsorption behaviors of macro-molecules could make it impossible to utilize triangle theory to obtain operating parameters. Moreover, triangle theory provides no rules to design salt profiles in iex-smb .

arxiv-2104-08015.title: On the Complexity of SHAP-Score-Based Explanations: Tractability via Knowledge Compilation and Non-Approximability Results
arxiv-2104-08015.creator: Marcelo Arenas marenas@ing.puc.cl, Pablo Barceló pbarcelo@uc.cl, Leopoldo Bertossi leopoldo.bertossi@skema.edu, Mikaël Monet mikael.monet@inria.fr
arxiv-2104-08015.description: Abstract Scores based on Shapley values are widely used for providing explanations to classification results over machine learning models. A prime example of this is the influential 𝖲𝖧𝖠𝖯 \mathsf{SHAP} -score, a version of the Shapley value that can help explain the result of a learned model on a specific entity by assigning a score to every feature.

arxiv-2108-08730.title: Accurate 3D frequency-domain seismic wave modeling with the wavelength-adaptive 27-point finite-difference stencil: a tool for full waveform inversion
arxiv-2108-08730.creator: Hossein S. Aghamiry, Ali Gholami, Laure Combe, Stéphane Operto
arxiv-2108-08730.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hossein S. Aghamiry, Ali Gholami, Laure Combe, Stéphane Operto. Efficient frequency-domain Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) of long-offset/wide-azimuth node data can be designed with a few discrete frequencies. However, 3D frequency-domain seismic modeling remains challenging since it requires solving a large and sparse linear indefinite system per frequency.

arxiv-2110-01811.title: On the Complementarity between Pre-Training and Back-Translation for Neural Machine Translation
arxiv-2110-01811.creator: Xuebo Liu, Longyue Wang, Derek F. Wong, Liang Ding, Lidia S. Chao, Shuming Shi, Zhaopeng Tu
arxiv-2110-01811.description: Abstract Pre-training (PT) and back-translation (BT) are two simple and powerful methods to utilize monolingual data for improving the model performance of neural machine translation (NMT). This paper takes the first step to investigate the complementarity between PT and BT.

arxiv-2407-11037.description: Abstract The model quantization technique of deep neural networks has garnered significant attention and has proven to be highly useful in compressing model size, reducing computation costs, and accelerating inference. Many researchers employ fake quantization for analyzing or training the quantization process.

arxiv-2503-10783.title: EEG-Based Decoding of Sound Location: Comparing Free-Field to Headphone-Based Non-Individual HRTFs
arxiv-2503-10783.creator: Nils Marggraf-Turley, Martha Shiell, Niels Pontoppidan, Drew Cappotto, Lorenzo Picinali
arxiv-2503-10783.description: Abstract Sound source localization relies on spatial cues such as interaural time differences (ITD), interaural level differences (ILD), and monaural spectral cues. Individually measured Head-Related Transfer Functions (HRTFs) facilitate precise spatial hearing but are impractical to measure, necessitating non-individual HRTFs, which may compromise localization accuracy and externalization.

arxiv-2606-15812.creator: Mahdi Mohammadigohari Mahdi.Mohammadigohari@gmail.com, Giuseppe Di Fatta giuseppe.difatta@unibz.it, Giuseppe Nicosia giuseppe.nicosia@unict.it, Panos M Pardalos pardalos@ise.ufl.edu

doe-osti-3002157-an-overview-of-the-molt.title: An Overview of the Molten Salt Thermal Properties Database–Thermophysical, Version 4.0 (MSTDB-TP V.4.0)
doe-osti-3002157-an-overview-of-the-molt.creator: Chesser, Ryan, Termini, Nick, Henderson, Shane et al.
doe-osti-3002157-an-overview-of-the-molt.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. A central repository of thermophysical and thermochemical properties of molten salt compositions of relevance to molten salt reactors (MSRs) is vital in supporting the broad community of MSR developers, who are at various stages of developing and deploying their reactor designs.

pmc-10674608.title: Long Non-Coding RNA as a Potential Biomarker for Canine Tumors
pmc-10674608.creator: Yan Zhang, Meijin Wu, Jiahao Zhou, Hongxiu Diao, Peter Bennett
pmc-10674608.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Simple SummaryCancer is the leading cause of death in dogs. Currently, researchers find long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) is a crucial regulator in the progression of various types of cancers. This article emphasizes the current and future advancements in lncRNAs as potential biomarkers for diagnosing, monitoring, and treating different types of canine tumors, which will benefit veterinary medicine as well as comparative medicine.AbstractCancer is the leading cause of death in both humans and companion animals.

pmc-10714487.title: Gut microbiota-related metabolite alpha-linolenic acid mitigates intestinal inflammation induced by oral infection with Toxoplasma gondii
pmc-10714487.creator: Jing Yang, Songhao Liu, Qian Zhao, Xiaobing Li, Kangfeng Jiang
pmc-10714487.description: BackgroundOral infection with cysts is the main transmission route of Toxoplasma gondii (T. gondii), which leads to lethal intestinal inflammation. It has been widely recognized that T. gondii infection alters the composition and metabolism of the gut microbiota, thereby affecting the progression of toxoplasmosis. However, the potential mechanisms remain unclear.

pmc-10873496.title: Meat protein alternatives: exotic species
pmc-10873496.creator: Óscar López-Campos
pmc-10873496.description: ral and political scenarios that are shaping the meat market, the production, and commercialization of meat from alternative species is expected to acquire a significant share of the market that is currently dominated by pork, poultry, beef, and lamb meats.

pmc-11322245.title: Feasibility of using diamond-like carbon films in total joint replacements: a review
pmc-11322245.creator: Anurag Roy, Annette Bennett, Lisa Pruitt
pmc-11322245.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Diamond-like Carbon (DLC) has been used as a coating material of choice for a variety of technological applications owing to its favorable bio-tribo-thermo-mechanical characteristics. Here, the possibility of bringing DLC into orthopedic joint implants is examined. With ever increasing number of patients suffering from osteoarthritis as well as with the ingress of the osteoarthritic joints’ malaise into younger and more active demographics, there is a pressing need to augment the performance and integrity of conventional total joint replacements (TJRs).

pmc-11430838.title: Comparative Performance of Autoencoders and Traditional Machine Learning Algorithms in Clinical Data Analysis for Predicting Post-Staged GKRS Tumor Dynamics
pmc-11430838.creator: Simona Ruxandra Volovăț, Tudor Ovidiu Popa, Dragoș Rusu, Lăcrămioara Ochiuz, Decebal Vasincu, Maricel Agop, Călin Gheorghe Buzea, Cristian Constantin Volovăț
pmc-11430838.description: Introduction: Accurate prediction of tumor dynamics following Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) is critical for optimizing treatment strategies for patients with brain metastases (BMs). Traditional machine learning (ML) algorithms have been widely used for this purpose; however, recent advancements in deep learning, such as autoencoders, offer the potential to enhance predictive accuracy.

pmc-11434197.title: Investigation of the Effect of Oxide Additives on the Band Gap and Photocatalytic Efficiency of TiO2 as a Fixed Film
pmc-11434197.creator: Mabrouka Ghiloufi, Tobias Schnabel, Simon Mehling, Salah Kouass, Barbara Pawelec
pmc-11434197.description: The effects of various additives (Y2O3, Ga2O3, and WO3) on photocatalytic degradation efficiency under UV light-emitting diodes (LEDs) and the optical properties of TiO2 Degussa P25 were investigated using ketoprofen and diclofenac, two non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs commonly detected in German rivers.

pmc-12573093.title: Magnesium Sulfate Combination Therapy for Aconitine‐Induced Electrical Storm
pmc-12573093.creator: Liujiang Ran, Jun Si, Yanyan Liu
pmc-12573093.description: We present the case of a 74‐year‐old man who developed 28 episodes of electrical storm secondary to aconitine poisoning from homemade herbal wine consumption, followed by complete recovery through 28 electrical cardioversions, hemopurification, and continuous magnesium sulfate infusion after 4 days.

pmc-12607389.title: Key Signals Produced by Gut Microbiota Associated with Metabolic Syndrome, Cancer, Cardiovascular Diseases, and Brain Functions
pmc-12607389.creator: Leon M T Dicks, Rui Vitorino
pmc-12607389.description: Gut microbiota have a significant impact neurotransmitters, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), immune signaling molecules, and gut hormones. These signaling molecules interact with receptors on the gut wall, immune cells, or the enteric nervous system (ENS), and reach the central nervous system (CNS) via the Vagus nerve (VN).

pmc-12767182.title: Deep learning-based diagnosis of temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis using whole-body bone scans
pmc-12767182.creator: Yeon-Hee Lee, Hee-Sung Kim, Seonggwang Jeon, Q-Schick Auh, Il Ki Hong, Sunju Choi, Fernando Guastaldi, Hyungsoon Im, Yung-Kyun Noh, Akhilanand Chaurasia
pmc-12767182.description: SummaryTemporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) is a degenerative condition that causes pain and functional limitation, yet its relationship with systemic osteoarthritis (OA) remains unclear. This study developed deep learning models to automatically diagnose TMJ-OA using bone scintigraphy (bone scans) and to evaluate systemic OA features as potential predictors.

pmc-13121460.title: Mechanical, tribological, and physical performance of sisal fiber reinforced epoxy composites filled with Aningeria, Cordia Africana, and Cedar Sawdust
pmc-13121460.creator: Jemanesh Girma Abay, Besufekad Negash Fetene, Gadisa Sufe
pmc-13121460.description: Composites are increasingly employed in aerospace, automotive, construction, sports, and defense industries owing to their high strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance, and customizable properties. This study focuses on sisal fiber reinforced epoxy composites with sawdust fillers from three Ethiopian hardwood species: Aningeria (Kerero), Cordia Africana (Wanza), and Cedar (Tid).

pmc-13389583.title: Phytochemical characterization and assessment of anti-leishmanial activity of Toona ciliata M. Roem leaf extract in Leishmania donovani infection
pmc-13389583.creator: Vishal Kumar Singh, Prasoon Madhukar, Rajneesh, Rahul Tiwari, Awnish Kumar, Shashi Bhushan Chauhan, Vibhav Gautam, Shyam Sundar, Rajiv Kumar
pmc-13389583.description: Leishmaniasis, a neglected tropical disease, affects millions of people globally. Various chemotherapeutic interventions have been employed for its treatment; however, the emergence of resistance in parasites and the adverse side effects associated with these medications have necessitated the screening of traditionally significant medicinal plants. We have investigated the phytochemistry screening, characterization, and in vitro anti-leishmanial activity of Toona ciliata M.

pmc-13436540.title: Visualisation and Prediction of Phosphate Deficiency via Auto‐Glowing Plant Bioluminescent Sensors
pmc-13436540.creator: Ching‐Wen Chiu, Ya‐Fen Zhan, Ting‐Yang Lu, Liang‐Jie Chiu, Ya‐Ru Li, Cheng‐Jiun Huang, Hao‐Jun Lu, Huai‐Ji Huang, Alexander S Mishin, Karen S Sarkisyan, Ting‐Ying Wu, Chiu‐Han Hsiao, Ming‐Jung Liu
pmc-13436540.description: Summary statementThis study introduces BioLumiPi, a novel, low‐cost, and non‐invasive biosensor plant, engineered by combining a phosphate (Pi) deficiency‐induced promoter with a fungal bioluminescence system in tobacco. BioLumiPi plants emit light that accurately reflects endogenous Pi deficiency and responds specifically to Pi levels.

pmc-13572833.title: The Effect of Extracorporeal Shockwave Therapy in Tendinopathy: A Systematic Review and Network Meta‐Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
pmc-13572833.creator: Ning‐Yi Guo, Si‐Qi Wang, Wei Liu, Zi‐Mu Mao, Jian‐quan Wang, Bing‐bing Xu
pmc-13572833.description: BackgroundIn recent years, numerous meta‐analyses have been published on the effectiveness of ESWT in treating various tendinopathies. However, due to limitations such as the small number of included studies, it remains unclear whether ESWT is definitively effective for all types of tendinopathies and what its comparative value is relative to other conservative treatments.
